key_finding: Compiled has lower actual wait in all 12 paired comparisons. Native has a lower measured window in short W1, short W8 and long W8; long W1 instead favors compiled (window C/N 0.96820). Do not claim universal native warm superiority.
recommended_results_paragraph: Starting from full Friendster compact CSR, compiled execution had lower launch-to-wait time in all 12 pairs across three fresh allocation blocks. With eight workers, short/long medians were 15.95/52.30 s for compiled versus 298.94/332.47 s for fresh file-backed native execution; median within-block C/N ratios were 0.0533/0.1573. Yet the long native measured window was faster (35.22 versus 38.23 s; paired ratio 1.086). Thus warm-window performance did not determine terminated-application ranking on this PVC. Native setup includes 29.42 GB promotion/fsync and a 524.87 MB private map per worker; common integrity scans, builds and post-exit checks remain outside application clocks. Variation is descriptive.

scope.claim: Actual E25 only; no predictive-quality or universal performance inference.

strongest_boundary_example.actual_wait: Native 298.9448 s vs compiled 15.9468 s; median paired C/N 0.0533436 (range 0.0520755–0.0546830).
strongest_boundary_example.sustained_example: long6400/W8: native window 35.2205 s vs compiled 38.2338 s (C/N 1.08556), but native wait 332.4713 s vs compiled 52.3019 s (C/N 0.157313).
strongest_boundary_example.window: Native 2.4071 s vs compiled 2.7646 s; median paired C/N 1.15348 (range 1.13881–1.20362).
